transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. I've never really been able to just sit idle, which, you know, usually isn't a terrible thing—I like being a hard worker! But, um, my customer service job recently changed to a new work setup, and... well, it's just made it a lot harder to hide that I can't really stay still. I really want to make sure I'm doing a good job and keeping my supervisors happy, so I thought I should finally ask someone about it. 

Is that the sort of thing you can help with?
Did you have this same difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Well, um... yes, I suppose I did. Looking back, this has probably been around long before my job changed. 

I remember in grade school... well, my teachers were always very kind, and they'd write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, which was always nice to hear! But they also... um, they'd mention that I could be a little careless sometimes. And that I talked out of turn. I really didn't mean to be a bother to them, I just got a little eager, I guess. They usually had to remind me to stay with my work and focus. I always tried my best to be good, though. 

I hope that's not too terrible for a kid? Is that the kind of information you were looking for, doctor?
In your everyday life and work now, do you often have trouble sustaining your attention or staying organized with your tasks?

Well, um... I really do try my absolute best to stay on top of everything. I want to be a good employee, you know? But, I suppose... well, maybe I do struggle a little bit sometimes. 

Like, when we have those longer coaching meetings with the supervisors, or if I have to read through a new customer service procedure... I always start off really well! I'm paying attention and trying to be a good listener. But then, after a few minutes, I... well, I realize my eyes are just kind of moving over the words, or I'm looking at the speaker, but I didn't actually take in what was just said. 

I always feel so bad when that happens, because I really don't want to seem disrespectful or like I don't care. I do care, very much! It's just... a little hard to stay locked in sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.

Well, um... I guess besides just the general feeling of needing to move, I do have some little habits. I really try to keep them quiet, though! I don't want to be a distraction to anyone else in the office. 

But, you know, even when I'm sitting there and I feel like I'm looking perfectly calm and collected... well, usually my foot is just bouncing away under the desk. Or, um, if we're in a meeting, I might find myself clicking my pen over and over. I honestly don't even realize I'm doing it half the time until someone looks over, and then I stop right away, of course! I always feel a little embarrassed when that happens. 

It's just a little nervous energy, I suppose. Is that... is that normal for someone my age? I hope it doesn't sound too silly.
Do you notice these same challenges affecting your life at home, or do they mostly happen at work?

Well, um... I guess it does happen a bit at home, too. I really try to be present and enjoy my downtime, especially with my wife, because she works hard and deserves a nice, relaxing evening. 

But... well, you know those quiet activities that are supposed to be relaxing? Like just sitting and reading, or watching a movie together on the couch? I always start out fine, but... I don't know, it just doesn't last very long before I'm shifting around, or making little comments about the movie, or suddenly remembering something I need to get up and check on. 

I try my best to just sit quietly so I don't ruin the movie for her, but it's like I just can't quite settle into it. I hope she doesn't think I'm not enjoying our time together, because I really am! I just... get a little restless, I suppose. Is that... is it okay that I struggle with the relaxing parts of the day, too?
